X1.evidence: Sec. 4.2: simulated participants received sampled demographic and relative-deprivation profiles (P); five completions per participant used temperature 1.0, while Study 1 ran ten blocks of 100 participants (repeats averaged across blocks, not analyzed as run variation).

X2.evidence: Secs. 3.3 and 4.3, Tables 4–7: outcome effects are quantified for experimental exposure or framing conditions, but no quantified outcome movement is attributed to varied simulation-uncertainty sources.

X3.evidence: Sec. 4.3, Table 7: reported interactions involve framing variables and participant relative deprivation; no interaction between simulation-uncertainty sources is estimated or shown.

notes: Study 2 varies simulated participant profiles (persona, P) and randomly assigns article framing, but article framing is the experimental condition and excluded as a source. Study 1 uses Latin-square balancing and repeated blocks to estimate ratings, not run-to-run variation.
